meta.name: Omada alert/event dictionary
meta.method: Notification-settings JSON (Global and Site), read-only. Per-instance fields (enable, email, webhook on/off) removed.
meta.webhookCapable: true when the controller exposes a per-type webhook flag for the key. TP-Link's Open API says that flag applies to Omada Pro controllers only; behaviour on software controllers is unverified.

entries.shortMsg: Global Logs Sent to Log Server
Sending Global Logs to Log Server Failed

entries.note: A broadcast/multicast storm crossed the storm-control threshold.
Switch loop detection fired. Loops can take down the whole LAN.
A switch port was blocked (loop prevention).
STP topology change (alert list). Shares its shortMsg with OSW_STP_FWD.
A WAN link went down.
PPPoE session to the ISP failed.
The gateway could not obtain a WAN IP (DHCP/PPPoE upstream problem).
Site-to-site IPsec tunnel went down.
ONU (fiber terminal) went offline. Appears in both lists. Only relevant with an Omada OLT.
ONU reported loss of power before going offline. Only relevant with an Omada OLT.
Daylight-saving-time configuration error; timestamps may be off.
The controller lost contact with an adopted device (AP, switch, gateway, OLT). Appears in both the alert and the event list.
The AP lost its wired uplink (often a mesh fallback). Clients on it may lose connectivity.
Device config no longer matches what the controller pushed. Appears in both lists.
The gateway's attack defense detected an attack (flood, scan and similar).
Gateway detected a stationary flood attack.
Gateway detected ARP conflicts (possible spoofing or a duplicate IP).
Gateway detected oversized ICMP (ping) traffic.

entries.shortMsg: The DHCP lease pool is exhausted
entries.note: A DHCP pool has no free leases; new clients can't get an address.

entries.shortMsg: A rogue DHCP server is detected
entries.note: Another DHCP server is answering on a gateway network. Common cause: a consumer router plugged in as a client.
Two hosts are using the same IP address.

entries.shortMsg: ONU Capability Failed to Match Profile
Automatic Add MAC Filtering Allow List Failed

entries.note: IntelliRecover started an automatic reboot to recover an AP.
IntelliRecover reboot did not bring the device back.
A device reported a monitored link down.

entries.shortMsg: Device informed monitor link internal error

entries.note: The gateway changed a LAN segment to avoid a conflict (for example with the WAN subnet).

entries.shortMsg: The mDNS rules are not working
entries.note: Configured mDNS reflection rules are not working.
A switch port was shut down by storm control.

entries.shortMsg: Switch Qos for Vlan Rule Exceeded

entries.note: Switch redundant power supply failure.
Switch fan failure.

entries.shortMsg: Mgmt Vlan DnsV4 Cleared Failed Alert.
Mgmt Vlan DnsV6 Cleared Failed Alert.

entries.note: Switch self-healing could not recreate the management VLAN. The only alert with level 'Critial' (sic) in the capture.
DHCP snooping on a switch flagged an untrusted DHCP server or packet.
ARP inspection on a switch flagged a suspicious ARP packet.

entries.shortMsg: Netif Healing Gate Recover Failed Alert.
Switch OUI Based VLAN rules exceeded the maximum simultaneous entry limit

entries.note: A switch firmware upgrade failed.

entries.shortMsg: LAN IP Is Conflict With Other Interfaces
entries.note: A gateway LAN IP overlaps another interface.
A switch or gateway changed its IP address.
DFS radar detected on a 5 GHz channel. The AP must vacate the channel, and connected clients drop or move.
An AP changed channel, usually auto-channel reacting to interference. Several in an hour on one AP suggests a crowded band.
A wireless client tried and failed to connect (wrong key, auth timeout, RADIUS, and similar). Bursts from one client often mean a saved wrong password or a weak-signal edge.
802.1X authentication failed on a switch port.
Traffic failed over to the backup WAN.
Gateway DHCP server messages (lease allocated/rejected). High volume.

entries.shortMsg: Site Logs Sent to Log Server
Sending Site Logs to Log Server Failed
entries.note: The controller failed to send site logs to the remote log server. Worth alerting on if syslog is your pipeline.

entries.shortMsg: Site Device List Schedule Mail Failed

entries.note: A device connected to the controller.
A device reconnected after a disconnect. Useful for measuring outage length with DEV_DISCONN.
The controller lost contact with an adopted device (AP, switch, gateway, OLT). Appears in both the alert and the event list.
ONU (fiber terminal) went offline. Appears in both lists. Only relevant with an Omada OLT.
The AP lost its wired uplink (often a mesh fallback). Clients on it may lose connectivity.
Device config no longer matches what the controller pushed. Appears in both lists.
The controller could not re-adopt a device automatically.
A client moved between APs; the line includes both APs and channels. Frequent back-and-forth roams point at overlapping coverage or a sticky client.
A wireless client left. The syslog line carries the SSID, AP, connected time and traffic, but no reason code or RSSI. Repeats in a short window are the main signal of flapping clients.
A wireless client joined (SSID, AP, channel). Pair it with W_C_DISCONN to measure session length.
A wired client went offline.
A wired client came online on a switch or gateway port.
Captive-portal authentication failed (wireless).

entries.shortMsg: Remembered Device Readopted After Factory Reset
entries.note: A previously known device was re-adopted after a factory reset.
IntelliRecover: the device is back online.
A previously detected loop has cleared.
STP port moved to forwarding (event list). Shares its shortMsg 'STP Topology Changed' with OSW_TOPO_C.
STP put a port into blocking.

entries.shortMsg: Netif Healing Not Exec Failed Alert.
Switch OUI Based VLAN rule applied

entries.note: A switch rebooted itself (for example after an upgrade).
Traffic is back on the primary WAN. TP-Link's guide calls this 'Primary WAN Recovered'.
